label: early original-phase step (t=2-4) after a prefix rich in p/2/h/u/r/o/k/m
predicate: (phase == 0) & (t >= 2) & (t <= 4) & (n_seen([tok("p"), tok("2"), tok("h"), tok("u"), tok("r"), tok("o"), tok("k"), tok("m")]) >= 2) & isin(in_tok, [tok("z"), tok("1"), tok("2"), tok("g"), tok("m"), tok("3"), tok("h"), tok("x"), tok("n"), tok("o")])
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase at positions t=2..5 (t=2-4 holds 97% of mass; t=3 peaks). It never fires at t=0-1, essentially never at the delimiter, and never in the copy phase. The position window alone gives about 97% mass recall but only 4% precision. Within the window, firing depends on which tokens came first. Prefixes containing p or 2 (as prev2_tok/first_tok, about 6-7x lift), and to a lesser degree h, u, r, o, k, m, raise the rate. The current input z, 1, 2, g, m, 3 also raises it (z gives 3.7x). The largest activations come from prefixes like "p p 2 X" / "r 2 2 X" / "2 p 2 X", peaking on the step right after a 2 at t=2. This looks like a graded, roughly additive token code over the first 2-3 tokens rather than a crisp rule: the best conjunction reaches dev F1 about 0.42, mass recall about 0.59.
